messages.author: 31159c9ecd804c46
messages.subject: Convergence failure in MCDS
parts:
Dear All:
I am fitting a half-normal key function with a single factor covariate using the MCDS analysis engine in Distance 7.3.  Convergence was not achieved, but the outcome resulted in the most parsimonious of the models I've tested.  I tried to achieve convergence by setting starting values for the three parameters in the model, but to no avail.

Regarding this, my question is, should I ignore the failure to converge and use the results obtained from fitting this model, or should I reject this model in favour of another (the second best option) which does converge?

Thanks and regards,
Stuart Cairns

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Convergence failure in MCDS
parts:
Stuart

When software fails to converge, this means the parameter estimates produced are not the maximum likelihood estimates, nor is the reported likelihood (and associated AIC value) the maximum likelihood.

If contrasting the AIC score of a model that did not converge with the AIC score of a model that did converge, you would not be comparing like with like.  Therefore I would suggest not using the results from the model that did not converge.  You would also want to investigate symptoms in the data the could result in models that do not converge.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Convergence failure in MCDS
parts:
Thanks for your prompt response to my query, Eric.  

Regarding symptoms in the data, I think I know what the problem is.  The factor covariate represents three different observers being used in a helicopter survey where only two were operating at any one time.  Compared with the other two, the third observer had a very small bit of the "action".  I think that this can be remedied by redefining the observers into two classes, i.e Observer 1 and Not_Observer 1.

Thanks again and regards, 
Stuart
